Author: Sanjay Kumar Singh

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 40192 of 2022
Applicant :- Mohit Awasthi

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Dheeraj Kumar Dwivedi Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State.

By means of this application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant, who is involved in Case Crime No.14 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, police station- Panki,
district- Kanpur Nagar, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.

As per prosecution case, in brief, informant, who is father of the deceased, has lodged an F.I.R.
against the applicant and his other family members with the allegation inter-alia that marriage of his daughter was solemnized two years back and he had given sufficient dowry, as per his capacity,
but, her in-laws were not satisfied and there was consistent demand of Rs. 5 lakhs and on non-fulfilment of the same, her daughter was being harassed and tortured in her matrimonial home.
On 16.01.2020 the applicant informed that his daughter has committed suicide.
It is contended by learned counsel for the applicant that, the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case as the cause of death is asphyxia due to antemortem hanging.

No other external injuries Mohit Awasthi vs State Of U.P. on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76769595/
1 were found on the body of the deceased.

sentences.text: The allegation of demand of dowry against the applicant is against the evidence on record.
Lastly, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that there is no chance of the applicant of fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 21.01.2020 and in case, he is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and cooperate with the trial.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that, in view of Section 113-A and B of the Indian Evidence Act, the presumption of dowry death shall be drawn against the applicant.
On account of abetment and harassment of the deceased by the applicant and his family members, she committed suicide.
It is also pointed out that, one prosecution witness has been examined before the trial Court, therefore, bail application of the applicant is liable to be rejected.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that, the victim died an unnatural death in her matrimonial home within a short span of about two years of her marriage.

Though, the deceased had died on account of hanging, but, it has come on record in the statement of PW-1 that, earlier, she was a rape victim, but, this fact was not in the knowledge of the applicant and her in-laws at the time of marriage and when the said fact was revealed, the accused persons started questioning about the same, due to which she felt herself humiliated and committed suicide.

Since one prosecution witness has been examined before the trial Court and trial is proceeding,
therefore, considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as keeping in view the submissions advanced on behalf of parties, gravity of offence, role assigned to applicant and severity of punishment, I do not find any good ground to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is rejected at this stage.
It is made clear that the observation contained in the instant order is confined to the issue of bail and shall not affect the merit of the trial.

However the trial court is directed to make an endeavour to conclude the trial, expeditiously,
without granting any unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties in accordance with provisions provided under Section 309 Cr.P.C.
Order Date :- 18.1.2023/
